project.name: fwupd

The line anchors below are resolved against that staged vulnerable tree, which still contains the unfixed `&&` length check at `libfwupd/fwupd-common.c:787-788` and matches the saved ASan frames in `fwupd_guid_from_string` and `fu_coswid_firmware_write`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42534694 (fwupd): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 2 found by fuzz target uswid_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42534694
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source in the ARVO workspace / static parse of the staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` in `fwupd_guid_from_string` while `uswid_fuzzer` processed the staged 74-byte witness. Static parsing of `gt_results/arvo_42534694/poc` shows the inner coSWID payload is a one-pair CBOR map whose `tag-id` text value begins `00002800-0000-0002800-00002800-00000`, then contains an embedded NUL and trailing padding bytes. `fu_coswid_read_string()` copies that full 48-byte text, but `fu_firmware_set_id()` stores it with `g_strdup`, so the surviving firmware ID is the 36-byte prefix `00002800-0000-0002800-00002800-00000`. During serialization `fu_coswid_firmware_write()` treats that non-NULL ID as a GUID candidate and passes it to `fwupd_guid_from_string()`. `g_strsplit()` turns the stored ID into section lengths `8-4-7-8-5`, but the vulnerable length check at `libfwupd/fwupd-common.c:787-788` uses `&&` instead of `||`, so the malformed third, fourth, and fifth sections are not rejected once the first two sections already match `8` and `4`. The function then still executes six fixed 2-byte tail copies from `split[4]`; when `i == 3`, `memcpy(buffer, split[4] + 6, 2)` starts at the end of the 6-byte `"00000\0"` allocation and produces the saved heap-buffer-overflow read. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by changing the section-length test to `||`, which rejects any malformed GUID field before the tail-copy loop.

source.description: First project statement on the vulnerable path that materializes the attacker-controlled coSWID `tag-id` text.
source.value_from: Static parsing of `gt_results/arvo_42534694/poc` shows the inner coSWID payload is a one-pair CBOR map whose `tag-id` value reaching this call is a 48-byte text string. Its first 36 bytes are `00002800-0000-0002800-00002800-00000`, followed by an embedded NUL and trailing padding bytes.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The fixed 2-byte copy from the last GUID field reads past the heap string allocated for `split[4]`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at this exact line, with callers `fu_coswid_firmware_write`, `fu_firmware_write`, and `fu_uswid_firmware_write`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The GUID section-length guard uses `&&` instead of `||`, so a candidate with only some malformed sections is accepted.
root_cause.note: For the stored ID from this witness, the split lengths are `8,4,7,8,5`; because the first two sections already satisfy the expected lengths, the whole condition is false and the malformed last field is not rejected. The patch changes these conjunctions to `||`.

parser_admitted.description: The inner coSWID payload decodes successfully and passes the root-map check, so the parser enters the map-walk loop at lines 548-610 where the `TAG_ID` string branch becomes reachable.

tainted_value_origin.description: This stores the malformed coSWID `tag-id` as the firmware ID that later reaches `fwupd_guid_from_string`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The 48-byte text materialized from the staged `poc` contains an embedded NUL after the 36-byte prefix `00002800-0000-0002800-00002800-00000`. `g_strdup` stops at that NUL, so the stored `priv->id` is exactly that 36-byte malformed GUID candidate.
tainted_value_origin.note: That stored prefix later splits into section lengths `8,4,7,8,5` in `fwupd_guid_from_string`.

fine_trace.note: Source step. On the staged payload, the map-walk has reached the `TAG_ID` branch and `pairs[i].value` is the 48-byte CBOR text value. `fu_coswid_read_string()` duplicates all 48 bytes, preserving the embedded NUL after the prefix `00002800-0000-0002800-00002800-00000`.

The parsed text from step 1 is stored as a C string. Because `g_strdup` stops at the first NUL byte, `priv->id` becomes the exact 36-byte prefix `00002800-0000-0002800-00002800-00000`; the later padding bytes do not survive.
During serialization the stored ID from step 2 is non-NULL, so the writer attempts GUID conversion on it before considering the plain-string fallback.
The string passed from step 3 is 36 bytes long because of step 2's NUL truncation, so this top-level format rejection is not taken and the malformed value is treated as a candidate GUID.

The candidate GUID is split into five heap strings with lengths `[8, 4, 7, 8, 5]`: `00002800`, `0000`, `0002800`, `00002800`, `00000`. The last token `split[4]` is a 6-byte allocation including its terminator, matching the ASan allocation stack from `g_strsplit`.

Root-cause step. Only `split[2]`, `split[3]`, and `split[4]` are malformed, so the `&&` chain evaluates false as soon as `split[0]` and `split[1]` match `8` and `4`. The function therefore fails to reject the `8-4-7-8-5` layout. The later `g_ascii_string_to_unsigned` calls on `split[0..3]` still succeed because those tokens are valid hex within the permitted numeric ranges, so control reaches the final tail-field loop.

The tail parser is hard-coded for six 2-byte chunks, i.e. a 12-hex-digit `split[4]`. With step 5's 5-character last field, iteration `i == 3` derives the source pointer `split[4] + 6`, which is the one-past-the-end pointer of the 6-byte allocation `"00000\0"`.

Sink. When step 7 reaches `i == 3`, this exact copy reads 2 bytes starting at `split[4] + 6`, immediately past the heap object for the last GUID field. The saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at this line and names `g_strsplit` / `g_strdup` as the allocation path.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch changes the exact section-length guard at `libfwupd/fwupd-common.c:787-788` from `&&` to `||`, so this witness's `8-4-7-8-5` split is rejected before the six-iteration tail-copy loop.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run fed the staged 74-byte witness to `uswid_fuzzer`; the valid outer uSWID wrapper exposes a coSWID `tag-id` text that is stored as `00002800-0000-0002800-00002800-00000`, and `fu_coswid_firmware_write()` later reaches `fwupd_guid_from_string()` on that malformed GUID candidate.

format.name: uSWID container with embedded coSWID `tag-id` text
format.contract: The witnessed trigger is the exact staged 74-byte uSWID file whose inner coSWID payload contains a one-pair CBOR map with a 48-byte `tag-id` text value. That text must begin `00002800-0000-0002800-00002800-00000`, contain an embedded NUL immediately after that 36-byte prefix, and therefore be stored by `g_strdup` as exactly the 36-byte malformed GUID candidate `00002800-0000-0002800-00002800-00000`. This exact stored prefix is required because it has total length 36 yet splits into section lengths `8,4,7,8,5`, which bypass the vulnerable `&&` length check and leave the last field too short for the six 2-byte copies in `fwupd_guid_from_string`.
